problem.title: Three Squares Around One Triangle
problem.statement: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. Squares are built on all three sides. A dissection shows the two leg squares exactly fill the square on the opposite side. What is the area of that opposite square?

solutionSteps.title: Square the legs
solutionSteps.body: The two leg-square areas are 3² = 9 and 4² = 16.

solutionSteps.title: Combine the areas
solutionSteps.body: 9 + 16 = 25 square units fill the opposite square.

validationMethods: independent 3-4-5 triangle audit: opposite side 5 gives square area 5²=25; option audit

problem.title: Is the Formula Authorized?
problem.statement: A triangle has two sides of lengths 7 and 9, but no angle measures or other constraints are given. Can its third side be determined using 7² + 9² = c²?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, because every triangle obeys the formula.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No, because no right angle is established.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because the two known sides are unequal.

hints: Two sides can meet at different angles.

solutionSteps.title: Check the gate
solutionSteps.body: The Pythagorean theorem applies only to a right triangle, with the legs meeting at 90°.

solutionSteps.title: Recognize freedom
solutionSteps.body: Changing the included angle changes the third side, so the given lengths alone do not determine it.

validationMethods: theorem-condition audit: no right angle is given
counterexample audit: varying the included angle between fixed sides 7 and 9 varies the third side, making only choice C valid

problem.statement: What is the distance between points (2,1) and (11,13)?

problem.title: Square on a Rectangle Diagonal
problem.statement: A rectangle measures 9 by 12. A square is built with the rectangle's diagonal as its side. What is the square's area?
hints: The rectangle sides and diagonal form a right triangle.
The requested square area is the diagonal squared.

solutionSteps.title: Answer the area question
solutionSteps.body: The square built on the diagonal has area d², so its area is already 225 square units.

validationMethods: side-square area identity directly gives diagonal-square area 9²+12²=225
independent length check: diagonal 15 from 9-12-15 triple, then square area 15²=225; options audited
